verdict.rationale: Neon's pricing page documents a free tier usable "with no time limits and no credit card required", and the GitHub README points users to the Neon Free Tier to create a serverless Postgres instance. A community user notes that usage-based billing without an always-on node suits a hobby project. The pack does not say how much the free tier allows, so whether it is "genuinely usable" for real prototypes rests on the vendor's claim plus one anecdote. Community complaints about the $20 minimum paid entry cost concern paid tiers, not the free tier. Missing for 10: documented free-tier quotas (compute hours, storage, branch and project limits), independent hands-on confirmation that real prototypes run within the free limits.

support.subject: As a founder, a genuinely usable free tier lets me run real prototypes before paying

citations.quote: Build and learn free with no time limits and no credit card required.
